title: AnchorGate v1.0: an anchored, seed-resolved evaluation protocol for spatiotemporal monthly precipitation prediction, with the benchmark it revises
description:
An evaluation protocol for data-driven spatiotemporal prediction, its reference implementation, and the precipitation benchmark it is applied to. The archive holds the model implementations, every analysis script that produces a number or figure in the accompanying manuscript, the per-seed prediction arrays and metric files those scripts consume, and the engineered feature set they read. Nothing needed to recompute a reported number is held back.

The protocol. Five components, each with a released implementation and each carrying a rule about what may be concluded: anchoring every architecture to reference baselines (persistence, a seasonal-naive predictor, a per-cell monthly climatology) scored on identical targets; a multi-seed feature-by-architecture factorial analysed as a randomised complete block, so that a difference is compared against the dispersion of the paired difference rather than the marginal spread of either arm; a decomposition of apparent ensemble gain into calibration and combination terms; a deseasonalised anomaly test, in the regime where climatology scores zero by construction; and spatially explicit diagnostics of the learned spatial prior, including an audit of the graph a graph model actually receives.

Model families. ConvLSTM (baseline, bidirectional, residual and attention variants); Fourier Neural Operators (pure FNO and an FNO-ConvLSTM hybrid decoder); Graph Neural Networks with Temporal Attention (GNN-TAT) with GCN, GAT and GraphSAGE encoders; a state-space (Mamba) variant; and a Late Fusion Ridge meta-learner over ConvLSTM and GNN-TAT predictions.

Case study and what the protocol returns. Boyacá, Colombian Andes, on CHIRPS v2.0 and SRTM (61×65 grid, 3,965 cells, 518 monthly steps from January 1982 to February 2025), seeds {42, 123, 456}, lead times 1 to 12 months. No architecture exceeds a per-cell monthly climatology, which attains pooled R²=0.730 and per-cell NSE 0.61 against 0.672 and 0.52 for the best ensemble at its most favourable value. The same anchoring step over eight further precipitation regimes returns a per-cell climatology between 0.454 and 0.896, so the result is a property of the problem rather than of this region. What the anchor bounds is what this model class extracts from precipitation history and static terrain: no model here receives an atmospheric or oceanic predictor, so it says nothing about predictability itself.

What is new in this release. A manuscript-numbers audit (manuscript_numbers_audit.py) binds every reported quantity to the file that produces it and fails when they disagree, when one quantity is stated two ways, when a withdrawn claim is left standing, or when a table's summary row is not the aggregate of its own rows. Running it established that several directories held more than one prediction array for the same model, and that different analyses were reading different ones; every path now names the seed, and the stratified tables, the spatial maps and the variograms are regenerated from one array per model. The fusion decomposition gained an arm that runs a single estimator under both fold schemes, which puts the cost of the fold defect at 0.003 in R² rather than the 0.015 previously attributed to it. The protocol carried a name in earlier drafts, first CeilBench and then AnchorBench, and carries none now: it is described by its five components and versioned by this deposit. The older provenance documents keep the earlier names because they are dated records.

Reference environment. Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.6.0 (CUDA 12.4), PyTorch Geometric 2.7.0, NumPy 2.1.3, SciPy 1.16.1, scikit-learn 1.7.1, xarray 2025.7.1. requirements-lock.txt pins every transitive dependency. Training was measured on one NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB; every analysis in this archive runs on CPU.

Scope. Archive accompanying the manuscript submitted to Geoscientific Model Development as a model evaluation paper. It supersedes the earlier deposits, which carried the code and none of its inputs because the release route excludes them, and whose GNN-TAT results were produced with the pre-correction graph and reported as best-seed values.
